reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a technical-support job listing with a Bangalore location, degree requirement, role qualifications, and an Apply Now flow. The sign-in and email verification steps are described as part of the application process, while the material does not establish that the page is unsafe or that information was misused. Requests to like or subscribe are ordinary channel engagement and are not linked to a financial or data-access condition.

citations.quote: I am bringing to you a very amazing job, here is the job of IBM the technical support associate
the process of applying will take little time so, we can talk about it as it can be difficult to apply
Your job location is- Bangalore
You have to have experience of at least 0 to 2 years In technical support role
so, first of all you will apply and click on the button

opening.argument: The video links a purported IBM employment opportunity to a concrete participation path: viewers are told to access the site, click the application button, register an email, and complete recruitment. The promised benefit is a technical-support job presented as available even to broad categories of applicants, while the required action is immediate account and contact-data submission. That is a classic low-barrier acquisition funnel: a valuable opportunity is used to motivate registration before the viewer can evaluate what will happen to the submitted information. The fact that the flow includes both email verification and a form makes the solicitation operational, not merely informational.

citations.quote: You can access the site in the description
first of all you will apply and click on the button
you can create an email by register the mail id
you can verify your email and you can complete job recruitment easily

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a job listing does not answer the concern that the video actively directs viewers into a registration and verification funnel. The reference statement describes the opportunity, but its own cited material confirms that viewers are instructed to click, register, and verify email. It also assumes those steps are ordinary without establishing that the particular flow is trustworthy or that the information request is necessary.

citations.quote: you can choose an entry field to connect but this is not compulsory
After entering your email details you can apply for the job recruitment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted steps show navigation through an application, not a cash or asset reward. The video does not promise payment for registering, and it does not show that information was misused. The opportunity itself is described as a technical-support position with stated qualifications, so the application action is connected to employment consideration rather than an unsupported giveaway.

citations.quote: You have to have experience of at least 0 to 2 years In technical support role
this is not compulsory
Your job location is- Bangalore

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the video directs viewers to an external site, presents the opportunity as unusually accessible, and walks them through email registration, verification, and a form containing personal fields. It also describes the application as easy to complete. Those elements create a low-friction path from a compelling job claim to collection of contact information, while the supplied material does not establish why each field is needed, who controls the receiving page, or what happens after submission. The screen sequence reinforces that viewers are being moved toward participation rather than given enough independent context to assess the offer.

citations.quote: https://careers.ibm.com/ShowJob/Id/889937/Technical%20Support%20Associate#?lang=en
you can apply for any degree or any particular year
you can verify your email

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats a displayed location and qualifications as if they resolve the risk signals, but those details do not explain the email-registration flow or the form shown after clicking. Nor does saying that a field is optional establish that the entire process is safe. The relevant issue is the combination of an easy-access opportunity and a directed external submission path, which the defense leaves unaddressed.

citations.quote: there is no requirement of any coding skill for you guys
you can choose an entry field to connect but this is not compulsory

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not evidence of deception by themselves. The supplied description identifies a careers.ibm.com URL, and the frames show an IBM-branded job page rather than an anonymous reward page. The video states that the role has qualifications and responsibilities; it does not promise effortless payment or claim that submitting information guarantees selection. The cited registration screens therefore show ordinary application mechanics, not misuse.

citations.quote: https://careers.ibm.com/ShowJob/Id/889937/Technical%20Support%20Associate#?lang=en
You have to be able to resolve customer issues
You have to have basic networking concepts

opening.argument: Although framed as an explanation of a vacancy, the video functions as promotional steering. It calls the opportunity “very amazing,” repeatedly encourages viewers to subscribe, directs them to the description, tells them exactly how to click through the application, and closes by asserting that recruitment can be completed easily. The practical effect is to convert attention into participation in a purported job-access process. Its broad eligibility language lowers hesitation, while the step-by-step instructions encourage viewers to submit an email and proceed before independently confirming the offer. That promotional funnel is consistent with scam-style solicitation even though it is wrapped in educational job-review language.

citations.quote: I am bringing to you a very amazing job
You can access the site in the description
you need to like this video and subscribe to its channel
you can complete job recruitment easily

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side calls the content a tutorial, but that does not negate its promotional mechanics. The video uses enthusiastic language, solicits channel engagement, and gives a step-by-step route into the application. A genuine location or qualification list can describe the offer without proving that the presenter’s funnel is safe or that viewers should trust the linked process.

citations.quote: the most amazing fact
please do subscribe to my channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotional tone and a subscription request do not establish a scam. The video identifies a specific technical-support role, location, experience range, and application route. Its instructions are consistent with helping viewers inspect and apply for a listed position, while nothing cited shows a fee, guaranteed hiring, guaranteed income, or a requirement to provide data as a condition of channel engagement.
